title: Unit normalization of the etale/pro-etale open-extension comparison
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and $A$ a finite discrete commutative ring. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ and $R_T=\nu_{T,*}$ for the comparison adjunction, $e=j_!^{et}$ and $d=j_!^{pro}$ for the two extensions by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], and $r=j_{et}^{-1}$ and $s=j_{pro}^{-1}$ for restriction. Let $\eta^e:1\to re$ and $\eta^d:1\to sd$ be their open-adjunction units. Let $a:C_Ur\xrightarrow{\sim}sC_X$ be the canonical inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and $c:C_Xe\xrightarrow{\sim}dC_U$ the canonical comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison].

The sectionwise identification $rR_X\cong R_Us$ induces, by the comparison and open adjunctions, natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_XeF,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,rR_XM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,R_UsM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(dC_UF,M).$$
These bijections send $h$ to $h\circ c_F^{-1}$. Moreover, for every etale $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $U$, the specified $c$ satisfies the unit normalization
$$s(c_F)\circ a_{eF}\circ C_U(\eta^e_F)=\eta^d_{C_UF}:C_UF\longrightarrow sdC_UF.$$
The comparison $a$ here is the canonical one above, not an independently chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09AF, label lemma-jshriek-comparison, proof by the common right adjoint; agent refinement recording unit normalization of the etale/pro-etale open-extension comparison

proof.text: Use the etale restriction identification and the pro-etale localization identification to regard $rG(W/U)$ as $G(W/X)$ and $sM(V/U)$ as $M(V/X)$. The etale identification for abelian sheaves is natural in $G$, hence commutes with every scalar endomorphism and holds for constant-$A$ modules. The pro-etale localization lemma supplies the constant-ring identification and the module restriction formula. The comparison definition gives $R_TM(W/T)=M(W/T)$ on etale objects and arrows. Thus both $(rR_XM)(W/U)$ and $(R_UsM)(W/U)$ are $M(W/X)$, with identical restrictions and scalar actions. Their identity maps define a natural $A$-linear isomorphism $\theta_M:rR_XM\to R_UsM$. These identifications use the canonical localization equivalences on chosen small skeleta; no geometric-stalk argument is used.

source.place: Tags 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison), 099R (section-comparison), and 09AE (definition-extension-zero); localization restriction on objects and arrows

proof.text: The two extension adjunctions and $C_T\dashv R_T$ give the displayed Hom chain, with middle arrow postcomposition by $\theta_M$; denote its composite by $\Psi_{F,M}$. It is a bijection natural in $F,M$, since every factor is one. Put $L_1=C_Xe$, $L_2=dC_U$, $Q_1=rR_X$, $Q_2=R_Us$. The composite-adjunction definition gives $L_i\dashv Q_i$. Apply the unit-normalized conjugation lemma with $\delta=\theta^{-1}:Q_2\simeq Q_1$ to get $\alpha:L_1\simeq L_2$. This is the canonical common-right-adjoint comparison of Tag 09AF, namely the $c$ in the statement: its right-adjoint identification is exactly the sectionwise identity just constructed, not an arbitrary isomorphism. The cited comparison theorem supplies its interpretation as the specified comparison between the two extensions.

source.place: Tag 09AF, proof by the common right adjoint; categories.tex Tags 0DV0 and 0B65 for composite adjunctions and conjugation

proof.text: The normalization in step 2 says that $\Psi_{F,dC_UF}(c_F)=1_{dC_UF}$. Indeed the $L_1$ adjunct of $c_F$ is $Q_1(c_F)\eta_{1,F}=\theta^{-1}_{L_2F}\eta_{2,F}$; applying $\theta$ and the inverse $L_2$ adjunction gives the identity. Naturality of $\Psi$ in its target, applied to $c_F^{-1}:dC_UF\to C_XeF$, gives $\Psi_{F,C_XeF}(1)=c_F^{-1}$. Applying the same naturality to $h:C_XeF\to M$ gives $\Psi_{F,M}(h)=h\circ c_F^{-1}$. This proves the first normalization by evaluating the Hom bijections.

source.place: Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints), naturality of the adjunction bijections

proof.text:
Write $J=j_{et,*}$, $K=j_{pro,*}$, $\iota:1\to Jr$ for the etale restriction/direct-image unit and $\lambda:rJ\to1$ for its counit. On the pro-etale site the inverse image $j_{pro}^{-1}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is not literally restriction: the open-unit evaluation lemma [lem-pur-proetale-open-unit-evaluation] gives the natural isomorphism $\rho:j_{pro}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}s$ onto localization restriction and states that, under $\rho$, the unit of $j_{pro}^{-1}\dashv K$ at $V/X$ is restriction along $V\times_XU\to V$. Transport this adjunction along $\rho$ to $s\dashv K$ with unit $\zeta:1\to Ks$; thus $\zeta_N(V)$ is that restriction map of $N$. The direct-image definitions give $\delta:R_XK\simeq JR_U$: at an etale $W/X$ both sides are the sections on $W\times_XU$, with the same arrows and coefficient actions. Moreover
$$\theta_N=\lambda_{R_UsN}\circ r(\delta_{sN})\circ rR_X(\zeta_N).$$
Evaluate at an etale $W/U$. Since $j$ is an open immersion, $W\times_XU\to W$ is the canonical isomorphism. By the open-unit evaluation lemma, $\zeta$ sends a section to its restriction along this projection. By the etale restriction lemma, $r(\iota)$ is restriction along the same projection; the triangle identity $J(\lambda)\iota_J=1$ then shows that $\lambda$ at $W/U$ is the inverse restriction, evaluating that section back on $W$. The map $\delta$ is the identity on these sections. The composite is therefore the identity of $N(W/X)$, exactly $\theta_N$ from step 1. Naturality on arrows and scalar endomorphisms gives the equality of module-sheaf maps.

source.place: Tag 099R (section-comparison), morphism/base-change description, and Tag 09AF; etale-cohomology.tex restriction-unit formula

proof.text:
The comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] is the conjugate $a^0:C_Ur\simeq j_{pro}^{-1}C_X$ of $\delta:R_XK\simeq JR_U$ under $C_Ur\dashv JR_U$ and $j_{pro}^{-1}C_X\dashv R_XK$: $\delta$ is induced by the identical base-change objects and arrows. With $s$ read as restriction, the $a$ of the statement is $\rho_{C_X}\circ a^0$, where $\rho$ is the identification of [lem-pur-proetale-open-unit-evaluation] used in step 4. Transporting the adjunction along $\rho$, $a$ is the conjugate of $\delta$ under $C_Ur\dashv JR_U$ and $sC_X\dashv R_XK$, the latter composed from $C_X\dashv R_X$ and the transported $s\dashv K$ with unit $\zeta$. Write $u_T:1\to R_TC_T$ for the comparison units. The composite-unit formula and the conjugation leaf give
$$JR_U(a_G)\circ J(u_{U,rG})\circ\iota_G
=\delta_{sC_XG}\circ R_X(\zeta_{C_XG})\circ u_{X,G}.$$
Apply $r$ and then $\lambda_{R_UsC_XG}$. Naturality of $\lambda$ and the triangle identity $\lambda_{rG}\circ r(\iota_G)=1$ reduce the left side to $R_U(a_G)u_{U,rG}$. Step 4 reduces the right side to $\theta_{C_XG}\,r(u_{X,G})$. Thus
$$R_U(a_G)\circ u_{U,rG}=\theta_{C_XG}\circ r(u_{X,G}).$$
This computes the compatibility with the specified $a$, rather than inferring it from existence of some pullback isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits) and 0B65; proetale.tex Tag 099R, inverse-image comparison from the identical direct-image square

proof.text:
For $h:C_XeF\to M$ its comparison adjunct is $R_X(h)u_{X,eF}$; its next, open adjunct is $r(R_X(h)u_{X,eF})\eta^e_F$. The middle member of the Hom chain is therefore
$$\theta_M\circ rR_X(h)\circ r(u_{X,eF})\circ\eta^e_F.$$
Naturality of $\theta$ and step 5 with $G=eF$ rewrite this as
$$R_U(s(h))\circ R_U(a_{eF})\circ u_{U,reF}\circ\eta^e_F
=R_U\bigl(s(h)\circ a_{eF}\circ C_U(\eta^e_F)\bigr)\circ u_{U,F}.$$
The equality is naturality of $u_U$ at $\eta^e_F$. Applying the inverse comparison adjunction shows that the $d\dashv s$ transpose of $\Psi_{F,M}(h)$ is $s(h)\circ a_{eF}\circ C_U(\eta^e_F)$. This directly calculates the four Hom bijections using their unit formulas.

source.place: Tag 0B65, Hom adjunct evaluated as unit followed by the right-adjoint image

proof.text: Set $M=dC_UF$ and $h=c_F$. Step 3 gives $\Psi(c_F)=1_{dC_UF}$, whose $d\dashv s$ transpose is $\eta^d_{C_UF}$. Step 6 computes that same transpose as $s(c_F)\circ a_{eF}\circ C_U(\eta^e_F)$, proving the unit normalization. Every map is natural, so the Hom bijections and both formulas have the asserted naturality. Only open localization and finite constant coefficients were used, including when $j=1$, $U=\varnothing$, $F=0$, or $A$ is the zero ring.
